setup.subtitle: Find the place that keeps sunlight for power and Earth in view for radio contact during your stay.

where.label: Where do you want to land?
where.coordsHint: Type the latitude, then the longitude, in degrees. Use a minus sign for south and west.
where.coordsError: Type the latitude (−90 to 90), a comma, then the longitude (−180 to 180).
where.error: Choose a place from the list, or type your coordinates.

when.label: When do you want to land?

stay.label: How long is your stay on the Moon?

hero.alt: The full Moon. NASA made this image from Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter data.
hero.credit: Moon image: NASA Goddard, from Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter data.

screen.error: Some data did not load, so a place can be missing. Check your connection, then reload the page.

copyLink.failed: The copy failed. Copy the link from the address bar.

site.loading: Calculating the positions of the Sun and Earth…
site.typedBody: The tool cannot calculate results for typed coordinates yet. Choose a place from the list at the top.
site.unknownBody: This place is not on our list. Choose a place from the list at the top.
site.missingBody: We have no hill data for this place yet. Set Hills to Ignored to see it with a flat horizon.

caveat.terrainNotModeled: The tool uses a flat horizon for this place. On the real ground, the Sun and Earth may be in view at different times.
caveat.approximate: This point represents a larger region.
caveat.horizonIncomplete: Our height map ends before the hills around this place end. The Sun and Earth may be hidden more often than the page shows.
caveat.terrainOff: The tool uses a flat horizon. On the real ground, the Sun and Earth may be in view at different times.

fit.fitsShort: Never more than 50 hours with no Sun and no Earth
fit.riskyShort: No Sun and no Earth from {{from}} to {{to}}
fit.riskyReason: This place has no Sun and no Earth from {{from}} until {{to}}. That is more than 50 hours in a row.

stay.day: The tool checked a stay of about 1 day.
stay.threeDays: The tool checked a stay of about 3 days.
stay.week: The tool checked a stay of about 7 days.
stay.twoWeeks: The tool checked a stay of about 14 days.
stay.month: The tool checked a stay of one full Moon day (29.5 days).

horizon.title: The sky from {{site}}
horizon.label: The view from {{site}}: the hills on the horizon, the Sun and the Earth.
horizon.legend: Thin lines: the paths of the Sun and Earth during the time span shown. Grey: the ground and hills.

countdown.title: Next
countdown.noChange: No change for one Moon day or longer

metrics.spanLunarDay: Over one Moon day from landing
metrics.sunVisible: Part of the Sun in view at the time shown
metrics.sunAbove: Height of the Sun above level ground at the time shown
metrics.sunBelow: Depth of the Sun below level ground at the time shown

timeline.title: When the Sun and Earth are in view
timeline.legend: Bar: in view. Gap: hidden. Frame: your stay.
timeline.summary_one: {{lane}}: in view {{count}} time during this time span.
timeline.summary_other: {{lane}}: in view {{count}} times during this time span.

playback.hint: An arrow key moves the time 1 hour. Shift and an arrow key move it 1 day.

credits.title: Data sources
credits.positions: Sun and Earth positions: astronomy-engine. We checked them against NASA JPL Horizons. The difference is less than 0.01°.
credits.hills: Hills: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter LOLA polar height maps (LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0, PDS Geosciences Node). The tool looks from 2 metres above the ground.
credits.checks: We checked the hills against PGDA 69 (Mazarico et al. 2011, average sunlight at the poles). Reference height map: PGDA 90 (Barker et al. 2023).

map.label: Map of the Moon's south pole with a marker for each place shown
map.labelEmpty: Map of the Moon's south pole. No places to show yet.
map.image: The ground at the Moon's south pole, drawn with shading
map.lowerBound: Our height map ends before the hills around this place end. The Sun and Earth may be hidden more often than the map shows.
map.offMap: {{site}} is too far from the pole to show on this map.
map.credit: Ground: NASA LRO LOLA height map, drawn with shading.

rank.pending: Comparing every south-pole place for your landing date and stay…
rank.failed: The tool could not compare the places, so there is no best option. Reload the page to try again.

why.only: The only place the tool could compare
why.closest: No place fits. This one is the closest.
why.onlyFit: The only one of {{count}} places that fits
why.dark: Shortest time with no Sun and no Earth, of {{count}} places
why.sunlight: Most sunlight among the best of {{count}} places
why.earth: Most time with Earth in view among the best of {{count}} places
why.tie: First of {{count}} places, equal with the next place
why.rules: The tool compares {{count}} south-pole places for your landing date and stay. A place that fits your stay comes first. Next, the tool prefers the shortest time with no Sun and no Earth. Then it prefers the most sunlight, then the most time with Earth in view.
why.leftOut: The tool does not compare {{site}}. Our height map ends before its hills end, so its numbers are upper limits only.

live.title: Live view
live.switch: Choose what the live view shows
live.mapHint: Each line points from a place to the Sun or Earth at the time shown.
live.loading: Calculating the positions of the Sun and Earth…
live.empty: The live view shows places that have results. Choose a place from the list at the top.

ranking.title: {{count}} south-pole places, best first
ranking.column: {{rank}}. {{site}}: {{verdict}}. Sunlight {{sun}}. Earth in view {{earth}}. Choose this place to compare it.
